scope: Official pinned EdgeTX v2.12.4 colour TX16S architecture; read-only review, no hardware execution

sources.claim: One lsWidgets VM initialized for all widget factories.
Every widget instance uses lsWidgets, separate zone/options registry refs.
create callback executes in lsWidgets; each instance gets separate context reference.
Standalone colour tools allocate independent lsStandalone VM.
Standalone disables widget refresh and pauses mixer/function scripts; close restores refresh.
Colour telemetry pop chooses current LuaScriptManager queue; managerless path falls back to global FIFO.
Each script manager allocates/registers, then unregisters/deletes, its receive queue.

conclusions.widgetGlobalRegistry: Can coordinate loaded widgets within the shared widget VM, unless caller deliberately supplies a different environment. AERODECK uses ordinary loadScript without env.
conclusions.crossToolWidgetRegistry: Cannot use Lua _G alone: standalone tool and widgets have separate Lua VMs.
conclusions.nativeTimerLease: Native model timer fields remain common outside either Lua VM; native lease can arbitrate explicit timer ownership.
conclusions.receiveQueue: Do not describe ordinary colour widget/tool managers as competing consumers of one global RX FIFO. They own registered queues; managerless APIs are a distinct fallback.
conclusions.remainingTransportCaution: Independent outgoing MSP requests can still contend for the physical link or confuse uncorrelated same-command exchanges if multiple clients are intentionally active. Foreground/background ownership remains useful; no transport change is recommended from VM facts alone.

canonicalEvidenceRole: New runtime evidence; frozen350-row baseline assessment is unchanged.
schedulingCaveat: Retained compact/hidden sampling and alarms depend on EdgeTX scheduling those widget callbacks. Opening a colour standalone tool disables widget refresh; close restores it. This is distinct from destroying the retained widget Lua state.
